did_you_know.text: Did you know? The ark of the LORD remained in Philistine territory for seven months after the Philistines took it from Israel.

Did you know? The Philistine priests and diviners said that the ark should not be returned empty-handed, but should be sent with a guilt offering—a gift expressing recognition of sin and the need for atonement.
Did you know? The Philistines made five golden tumors and five golden mice, corresponding to the number of Philistine rulers, because the plague had struck the entire region and its leaders.
Did you know? The Philistine priests reminded their people of Egypt and Pharaoh, warning them not to harden their hearts as the Egyptians had done, until they were forced to let Israel go.
Did you know? To test whether the plague had come from the LORD, the Philistines proposed using a new cart and two cows that had never been yoked, while leaving their calves at home.

Did you know? The Philistines set a test: if the cart went up the road to Beth-shemesh, they would recognize that the LORD’s hand had caused the plague; if not, they would conclude that it had happened by chance.
Did you know? The cows went straight toward Beth-shemesh, without turning right or left, even though their calves had been left behind; the Philistine rulers followed them as far as the border.
Did you know? At that time, the people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the ark, they rejoiced greatly.

Did you know? The Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the box containing the golden objects from the cart and placed them on a large stone, and the people of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrifices to the LORD.

Did you know? After the plague at Beth-shemesh, the people recognized the holiness of the ark and the awe involved in standing before the LORD, so they asked that it be transferred to the people of Kiriath-jearim.
